output.impression: 1. Extensive bilateral gyriform cortical restricted diffusion (cortical ribboning), left greater than right. 2. Restricted diffusion and FLAIR hyperintensity in the caudate nuclei and putamina, with milder dorsomedial thalamic restriction; no pulvinar predominance. 3. Diffuse cortical volume loss. 4. No hemorrhage, mass lesion, territorial infarct or abnormal enhancement. The combination of cortical ribboning with deep gray nuclei restricted diffusion is characteristic of prion disease; status epilepticus and hypoxic injury can produce cortical diffusion restriction and cannot be excluded on imaging alone. Clinical correlation recommended.

alternatives: Levetiracetam and lacosamide have no appreciable hERG effect; lacosamide prolongs the PR interval rather than the QT interval.
interactions: Quetiapine + escitalopram: both prolong the QT interval through hERG channel blockade; additive risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes. Obtain an ECG and check potassium and magnesium; reduce or stop one agent if QTc exceeds 500 ms.
Levetiracetam + quetiapine, escitalopram or lisinopril: no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interaction; levetiracetam is renally cleared.
Lorazepam + quetiapine: additive sedation and respiratory depression; monitor the airway after each dose.
Valproate + quetiapine: modest rise in quetiapine exposure with additive sedation; the combination is associated with neutropenia, so monitor the blood count.
Fosphenytoin or phenytoin + quetiapine and escitalopram: CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 induction substantially lowers the exposure of both.
output.proposed: Lorazepam, levetiracetam, valproate, fosphenytoin or lacosamide with quetiapine, escitalopram and lisinopril

output.query: Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease diagnostic criteria, CSF biomarkers and EEG patterns

results.finding: Current diagnostic criteria for probable sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease combine rapidly progressive dementia and typical clinical features with a positive RT-QuIC assay, a characteristic MRI pattern of cortical and striatal diffusion restriction, or periodic sharp wave complexes on EEG; RT-QuIC has high specificity, and 14-3-3 and total tau are less specific surrogate markers of rapid neuronal loss.

Generalized periodic discharges and electrographic seizures are separate patterns with separate definitions; a seizure requires evolution in frequency, morphology or location, or a clinical correlate, which an invariant periodic pattern lacks.

In patients with an encephalopathy, periodic discharges at 2.5 Hz or less meet criteria for non-convulsive status epilepticus only with typical spatiotemporal evolution, subtle ictal clinical phenomena or improvement after IV antiseizure medication.
Continuous EEG for at least 24 hours is recommended when non-convulsive seizures are suspected in a patient who does not regain consciousness after a convulsion.

output.summary: Probable sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease is defined by rapidly progressive dementia with a positive RT-QuIC assay, a characteristic MRI pattern or periodic sharp wave complexes; RT-QuIC is the most specific of these markers [Hermann_2021]. Periodic discharges and electrographic seizures are distinguished by evolution and clinical correlates [ACNS_2021; Salzburg_NCSE_2015], and continuous EEG for at least 24 hours is recommended when consciousness does not return after a convulsion [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Glucose 102 mg/dL, venous lactate 3.4 mmol/L and CK 412 U/L after a convulsion; electrolytes, magnesium, renal and hepatic function normal; toxicology negative: no reversible metabolic or toxic cause
action_criteria.label: Emergency laboratory work-up: glucose, CBC, electrolytes, magnesium, renal and hepatic function, toxicology screen
action_criteria.rationale: Glucose, electrolyte, renal and hepatic derangements are reversible causes of seizures and decide the ASM and its dose; a toxicology screen because this is a first seizure in a patient on psychotropic drugs [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Diffuse cortical atrophy beyond that expected for age; no hemorrhage, mass, midline shift or hydrocephalus
action_criteria.label: Non-contrast head CT after stabilization
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes hemorrhage, mass or edema that would change management, and must precede the lumbar puncture [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Two distinct patterns: invariant generalized periodic sharp wave complexes at 0.8-1.2 Hz, and superimposed recurrent left temporal (T3, T5) electrographic seizures with spatiotemporal evolution, lasting 15 to 30 seconds every 3 to 5 minutes
action_criteria.label: Continuous video-EEG to separate the periodic pattern from superimposed seizures and monitor treatment
action_criteria.rationale: Failure to regain consciousness 90 minutes after a convulsion needs EEG confirmation of ongoing seizures; continuous monitoring for at least 24 hours [Brophy_2012]; terminology [ACNS_2021].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Bilateral gyriform cortical restricted diffusion (left greater than right) with caudate and putaminal restriction, milder dorsomedial thalamic restriction and FLAIR hyperintensity; no mesial temporal change, infarct or enhancement
action_criteria.label: MRI brain with DWI and FLAIR for the cause of the rapidly progressive dementia and new seizures
action_criteria.rationale: New-onset status epilepticus on a rapidly progressive dementia needs MRI; the outside study is not available here, and the cortical and striatal diffusion pattern is one of the diagnostic markers of prion disease while also excluding encephalitis and a structural lesion [Hermann_2021; Glauser_2016].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum LGI1, CASPR2, NMDAR and GABA-B antibodies negative; anti-thyroid peroxidase 18 IU/mL, normal
action_criteria.label: Serum autoimmune encephalitis antibody panel (LGI1, CASPR2, NMDAR, GABA-B) with anti-thyroid peroxidase
action_criteria.rationale: Autoimmune encephalitis is the treatable mimic of rapidly progressive dementia with seizures, and serum is the more sensitive specimen for LGI1 and CASPR2 [Graus_2016].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Acellular CSF with normal protein and glucose; HSV PCR not detected and CSF antibody panel negative; 14-3-3 positive, RT-QuIC positive and total tau 12840 pg/mL
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture: cell count, protein, glucose, HSV PCR, CSF autoimmune panel, 14-3-3, RT-QuIC and total tau
action_criteria.rationale: CSF excludes the treatable mimics (herpes encephalitis, antibody-mediated encephalitis) and RT-QuIC is the specific marker of prion disease; it is recommended rather than required because the clinical picture, MRI and EEG already meet the criteria for probable disease and the result does not change acute management [Hermann_2021; Tunkel_2008].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Quetiapine with escitalopram gives additive QT prolongation (ECG, potassium and magnesium advised); levetiracetam has no relevant interaction; enzyme-inducing ASMs would lower the exposure of both psychotropics
action_criteria.label: Drug-interaction check of the candidate ASMs against quetiapine and escitalopram
action_criteria.rationale: Her quetiapine and escitalopram prolong the QT interval together and are induced or displaced by some ASMs, which narrows the sensible choice; no single interaction forbids the first-choice drug, so the check is recommended [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on RT-QuIC, 14-3-3 and total tau, and on the EEG definitions of periodic discharges and electrographic seizures
action_criteria.label: Literature on prion disease diagnostic criteria and biomarkers
action_criteria.rationale: Optional background on the diagnostic markers and on separating periodic discharges from seizures; it is not a clinical step [Hermann_2021].

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat the generalized periodic sharp wave complexes as seizures; they are invariant and have no clinical correlate.
Do not escalate to an anaesthetic infusion with intubation for the focal seizures without a goals-of-care discussion in probable prion disease.
Do not accept prion disease as the final diagnosis before the treatable mimics (herpes encephalitis, antibody-mediated encephalitis) are excluded.
required_recommendations: Treat the recurrent left temporal electrographic seizures, not the periodic pattern: IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg (maximum 4 mg per dose, repeat once after 5 to 10 minutes) [Glauser_2016].

Load a second-line ASM: IV levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (maximum 4500 mg); prefer it to fosphenytoin, whose enzyme induction lowers quetiapine and escitalopram exposure, and to valproate, which adds sedation with quetiapine [ESETT_2019].
Continue video-EEG for at least 24 hours to confirm that the electrographic seizures have stopped and that the periodic pattern is unchanged [Brophy_2012].
Correct and keep potassium and magnesium in the normal range and obtain an ECG before any further QT-prolonging drug, given quetiapine with escitalopram.
Complete the exclusion of treatable mimics (CSF HSV PCR and CSF antibody panel) before accepting prion disease as final [Graus_2016; Tunkel_2008].

Hold a goals-of-care discussion with the son and involve palliative care, and limit escalation to what keeps her comfortable; prion disease is uniformly fatal and no disease-modifying treatment exists.

Apply standard precautions, and use the prion-specific instrument and tissue handling policy for any invasive procedure or if autopsy is discussed; inform the laboratory that CSF is from a patient with suspected prion disease.

avoided_actions.rationale: No clinical suspicion of cardiac source of embolus or cardiogenic seizure; routine echo is not indicated in SE workup absent cardiac findings.
No suspicion of arrhythmogenic syncope or cardiac comorbidity precipitating SE; routine telemetry beyond standard ICU monitoring adds cost without yield.
Amyloid PET has no role in acute SE evaluation; dementia biomarker imaging does not change acute management.
Carotid duplex is for ischemic stroke workup; SE without focal vascular suspicion does not warrant carotid imaging.
Polysomnography studies sleep disorders and has no role in the acute evaluation of status epilepticus.
A neuropsychological battery cannot be performed in an unresponsive patient.

accepted: Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease with superimposed focal left temporal non-convulsive status epilepticus on a background of typical periodic sharp wave complexes

differential.diagnosis: Myoclonus and periodic discharges of prion disease alone, without superimposed seizures
differential.key_features: The periodic pattern is invariant and has no clinical correlate, but the EEG also shows recurrent left temporal runs with spatiotemporal evolution, which are seizures
The treatable mimic of rapidly progressive dementia with seizures, but serum and CSF antibody panels are negative, the CSF is acellular and RT-QuIC is positive
Temporal seizures raise it, but there is no fever, the CSF is acellular, HSV PCR is not detected and the MRI shows no mesial temporal change
Sporadic disease is by far the most common; no family history and no pulvinar-predominant pattern on MRI
Quetiapine could explain jerking, but not the cortical and striatal diffusion restriction, the periodic discharges or the positive RT-QuIC
Triphasic periodic discharges occur in metabolic encephalopathy, but electrolytes, renal and hepatic function are normal and the toxicology screen is negative

key_clinical_evidence: Generalized periodic sharp wave complexes are a supportive marker of sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, not seizures; an invariant periodic pattern without a clinical correlate is not treated as status epilepticus [ACNS_2021; Hermann_2021].

A second pattern on the same recording can be ictal: runs with evolution in frequency, morphology or field are electrographic seizures and are treated, whatever the background disease [Salzburg_NCSE_2015].
RT-QuIC is the most specific CSF marker of prion disease; 14-3-3 and total tau reflect rapid neuronal loss and are far less specific [Hermann_2021].
Antibody-mediated encephalitis is the treatable mimic of rapidly progressive dementia and must be excluded before prion disease is accepted [Graus_2016].
Prion disease is uniformly fatal: the extent of escalation for seizures is a goals-of-care decision, while symptomatic seizure treatment remains appropriate for comfort.

patient.history_present_illness: A 67-year-old White right-handed woman, a retired teacher, was brought to the emergency department by her son after a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure, her first ever, followed by failure to return to normal consciousness over 90 minutes. Over 3 months she has declined from mild cognitive complaints to being unable to recognize her son and needing full-time care, with startle myoclonus and an unsteady gait. Her neurologist has been investigating prion disease and considered sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease probable; a brain MRI 4 weeks ago and an EEG at another hospital were part of that work-up, and no specific treatment was started because none exists. The outside EEG report, which the son has with him, reads 'generalized periodic sharp wave complexes at 1 Hz, typical CJD pattern, highly supportive of prion disease'; the imaging report is not available at this hospital. She takes quetiapine for behavioral symptoms and escitalopram for depression that predates the dementia. On arrival she is unresponsive, making occasional groaning sounds, with intermittent irregular jerking of both arms. Her son asks whether the jerking needs treatment or whether it is 'just the CJD'.

neurological_exam.additional: No neck stiffness. No tongue laceration. No incontinence recorded by the paramedics. Standard precautions in place.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 3 mm bilaterally, sluggishly reactive. Blink reflex present. Oculocephalic reflex present. No gag reflex.
neurological_exam.mental_status: GCS 5 (E2 V1 M2). Eyes open briefly to pain only, no verbal response, extensor posturing to noxious stimulation 90 minutes after the convulsion.
neurological_exam.motor: Irregular myoclonic jerks of both arms, not rhythmic and not stimulus-locked on observation. No purposeful movement. Diffusely increased tone with bilateral extensor posturing to pain.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Diffusely brisk reflexes bilaterally. Bilateral Babinski present.
